objects.description: Abstract base class in namespace mesh that models hardware-specific operations of the main device/board. It provides battery voltage reading, ADC calibration, manufacturer name, TX hooks, reboot/power control, GPIO access, startup reason, and optional OTA update initiation. It is an interface (has pure virtuals) and is intended to be subclassed by platform-specific implementations.

Abstract base class in namespace mesh that represents a real-time clock. It exposes pure virtual methods to get and set the current UNIX time, an optional tick method for periodic updates, and provides a helper getCurrentTimeUnique() that ensures monotonically increasing time values across successive calls.

Abstract random number generator interface in the mesh namespace. Implementations must provide random() to fill a buffer with sz bytes. nextInt() is a convenience method that returns a uniformly distributed uint32 in [_min, _max) based on the underlying random(). Construction is via user-defined subclasses; this header does not define any concrete constructors or ownership patterns.

Static utility class in the mesh namespace providing cryptographic and formatting helpers: SHA-256 hashing (single or two-fragment), AES-128 encrypt/decrypt, encrypt-then-MAC and verify-then-decrypt, hex encoding/decoding, hex printing to a Stream, and text parsing by separator. The class is non-instantiable in practice since all members are static; construction is not intended or required.

Fundamental transmission unit in the mesh namespace. Encapsulates header bitfields (route type, payload type, payload version), optional transport codes, a routing path buffer, payload buffer, and an SNR value. Provides helpers to compute a payload hash, query header fields, mark packets non-retransmittable, compute raw/wire length, and serialize/deserialize to a byte blob. Construction is via default constructor; destruction is trivial (no ownership beyond in-class arrays). Constants like MAX_PATH_SIZE, MAX_PACKET_PAYLOAD, and bit masks are expected from included headers. Details of serialization format and hash algorithm are not present here.

Represents a mesh participant identified by an Ed25519 public key. Provides signature verification, key/hash comparison helpers, and binary/stream I/O. Construction accepts empty, hex public key, or raw key buffer. Destruction/ownership details are standard (no dynamic ownership). Sizes like PUB_KEY_SIZE and PATH_HASH_SIZE are external constants not defined here.

Device-owned identity that holds both Ed25519 private and public keys. Adds signing and ECDH (X25519 from Ed25519) shared-secret derivation, plus stream and raw-buffer serialization helpers. Holds private key inline as PRV_KEY_SIZE bytes; callers must protect instances carefully. Exact RNG and key-size constants are external.

Abstract interface for a millisecond-resolution clock. Implementations must provide getMillis() that returns an ever-increasing millisecond tick. Used by Dispatcher for timing/scheduling. Details such as epoch and overflow handling are not specified in this header.

Abstract interface for a packet radio used by the mesh stack. Implementations handle RX/TX of raw frames, airtime estimation, signal metrics, and operational state (receive mode, AGC, noise floor). Several methods have default no-op implementations; core operations are pure virtual.

Abstract manager for Packet allocation and queuing. Provides a pool interface (alloc/free) and inbound/outbound queue operations with priorities and scheduling timestamps. Implementations define ownership semantics for Packet instances; this header assumes the manager owns allocated Packets once queued.

Core orchestrator that coordinates Radio I/O, PacketManager queues, and time via MillisecondClock. It schedules transmissions, processes receptions, tracks airtime and stats, and exposes hooks for subclasses to implement policy (onRecvPacket, logging, timing parameters). Constructed with references to Radio, MillisecondClock, and PacketManager; lifetime/ownership of those are external.

objects.description: Type alias for a 32-bit action code returned by Dispatcher hooks (e.g., onRecvPacket). Encodes actions such as release/hold/retransmit, often with parameters packed into bits via macros in this header.

Lightweight POD class holding a group channel identifier and its shared secret. The hash uniquely identifies the channel (size PATH_HASH_SIZE). The secret stores the group key material (size PUB_KEY_SIZE). Used by Mesh for matching and decrypting group messages.

Abstract interface for packet bookkeeping (e.g., duplicate suppression). Implementations must define hasSeen() to detect previously processed packets and clear() to remove entries. No ownership semantics are specified here; lifetime managed by user. Details of Packet and hashing are external to this header.

High-level mesh networking node built atop Dispatcher. Provides packet receive routing, duplication control via MeshTables, timing via RTCClock, randomness via RNG, and a suite of virtual hooks for handling different payload types (peer data, paths, trace, group, control, raw). Also offers factory methods to create and send various packet types and routing modes. Ownership: Mesh stores non-owning pointers to RNG, RTCClock, and MeshTables provided at construction. Subclass to implement behavior; many methods are virtual and some pure-virtual are inherited from Dispatcher. External dependencies like Dispatcher, Packet, Identity, Radio, etc., are declared elsewhere.

functions.name: mesh::RTCClock::getCurrentTime

functions.name: mesh::RTCClock::getCurrentTimeUnique

Uniqueness guarantee is per-instance and per-process; not synchronized across devices or restarts.

functions.name: mesh::RNG::random
functions.signature: virtual void mesh::RNG::random(uint8_t* dest, size_t sz) = 0;
functions.description: Fills dest with sz bytes of cryptographically strong random data. This is a pure virtual interface that must be implemented by RNG subclasses; used as the underlying entropy source for higher-level methods like nextInt.
requirements: dest must be a valid, writable buffer of at least sz bytes.
sz may be zero; if non-zero, dest must not be null.
Must be implemented by a concrete subclass before being called (pure virtual).
Thread-safety and determinism are unknown; callers should not assume either.

functions.name: mesh::RNG::nextInt
functions.description: Returns a random 32-bit integer in the half-open interval [_min, _max). Uses the RNG’s random() implementation as the source of bytes. Intended for simple bounded random selection.
requirements: _min must be less than _max (otherwise the range is empty/invalid).
The underlying random(uint8_t*, size_t) must be implemented and functional for this RNG instance.
Distribution and bias characteristics are unspecified; callers should not assume perfect uniformity if implementation details are unknown.

functions.name: mesh::Utils::sha256
functions.signature: static void mesh::Utils::sha256(uint8_t* hash, size_t hash_len, const uint8_t* msg, int msg_len);
functions.description: Computes the SHA-256 hash of a single message buffer msg and writes up to hash_len bytes into hash (truncated if hash_len < 32). Use when hashing a contiguous message.
requirements: hash must point to a writable buffer of at least hash_len bytes.
hash_len may be from 0 up to 32 bytes (SHA-256 output size). Values >32 will result in truncation to 32; behavior for >32 is unspecified by the comment, so callers should keep it <=32.
msg_len must be >= 0. If msg_len == 0, msg may be null; otherwise msg must point to at least msg_len bytes.
Function performs a raw SHA-256 without a key (not an HMAC).

functions.name: mesh::Utils::sha256
functions.signature: static void mesh::Utils::sha256(uint8_t* hash, size_t hash_len, const uint8_t* frag1, int frag1_len, const uint8_t* frag2, int frag2_len);
functions.description: Computes the SHA-256 hash of two message fragments concatenated in order (frag1 || frag2) and writes up to hash_len bytes into hash (truncated if hash_len < 32). Use when data is split in two buffers.
requirements: hash must point to a writable buffer of at least hash_len bytes.
hash_len may be from 0 up to 32 bytes (SHA-256 output size).
frag1_len and frag2_len must be >= 0. If a length is 0, its pointer may be null; otherwise the pointer must reference at least the given length.

functions.name: mesh::Utils::encrypt
functions.signature: static int mesh::Utils::encrypt(const uint8_t* shared_secret, uint8_t* dest, const uint8_t* src, int src_len);
functions.description: Encrypts src using AES-128 with shared_secret as the key. Pads the final block with zero bytes. Writes ciphertext to dest and returns the ciphertext length in bytes (rounded up to the AES block size, 16 bytes). Key length is fixed at CIPHER_KEY_SIZE.
requirements: shared_secret must point to a key of exactly CIPHER_KEY_SIZE bytes (value of CIPHER_KEY_SIZE is defined elsewhere).
src_len must be >= 0. If src_len == 0, src may be null; otherwise src must point to at least src_len bytes.
dest must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the ciphertext: at least ((src_len + 15) / 16) * 16 bytes (AES block size is 16).
Padding scheme is zero-padding; callers must account for potential ambiguity when plaintext ends with zero bytes if they later strip padding.

functions.name: mesh::Utils::decrypt
functions.signature: static int mesh::Utils::decrypt(const uint8_t* shared_secret, uint8_t* dest, const uint8_t* src, int src_len);
functions.description: Decrypts src using AES-128 with shared_secret as the key. Expects src_len to be a multiple of the AES block size (16). Writes plaintext to dest and returns the number of bytes written; trailing zero bytes may remain in the final block due to zero-padding.
requirements: shared_secret must point to a key of exactly CIPHER_KEY_SIZE bytes (value defined elsewhere).
src_len must be >= 0 and must be a multiple of 16 (AES block size).
src must point to at least src_len bytes if src_len > 0; may be null if src_len == 0.
dest must point to a writable buffer large enough for src_len bytes (ciphertext length).
Caller is responsible for handling/stripping any trailing zero padding in the final block if needed.
Function does not authenticate data; ciphertext integrity must be ensured by the caller or by using MACThenDecrypt.

functions.name: mesh::Utils::encryptThenMAC
functions.signature: static int mesh::Utils::encryptThenMAC(const uint8_t* shared_secret, uint8_t* dest, const uint8_t* src, int src_len);
functions.description: Encrypts src (AES-128 with zero-padding) and then computes a MAC over the ciphertext, placing the MAC in the leading bytes of dest followed by the ciphertext. Returns the total length (MAC + ciphertext). Intended for combined confidentiality and integrity.
requirements: shared_secret must point to a key of exactly CIPHER_KEY_SIZE bytes (value defined elsewhere).
src_len must be >= 0. If src_len == 0, src may be null; otherwise src must point to at least src_len bytes.

dest must be large enough to hold MAC_length + ((src_len + 15)/16)*16 bytes. The exact MAC_length is not documented here and is unknown; callers must consult the implementation or associated constants.
The specific MAC algorithm and tag length are unspecified in the header; callers must not assume a particular tag size or construction.

functions.name: mesh::Utils::MACThenDecrypt
functions.signature: static int mesh::Utils::MACThenDecrypt(const uint8_t* shared_secret, uint8_t* dest, const uint8_t* src, int src_len);
functions.description: Verifies the MAC in the leading bytes of src and, if valid, decrypts the remaining bytes (AES-128, zero-padding) into dest. Returns 0 if the MAC is invalid; otherwise returns the length of decrypted bytes written to dest.
requirements: shared_secret must point to a key of exactly CIPHER_KEY_SIZE bytes (value defined elsewhere).
src must contain a leading MAC tag followed by ciphertext whose length is a multiple of 16; exact MAC tag size is unspecified here.
src_len must be at least MAC_length + 0 and the ciphertext portion (src_len - MAC_length) must be a multiple of 16. MAC_length is unknown from this header; consult implementation/constants.
dest must be large enough to hold the decrypted plaintext for the ciphertext portion.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates MAC verification failed; positive value indicates decrypted length. Any trailing zero padding in the last block may need to be handled by the caller.

functions.name: mesh::Utils::toHex
functions.signature: static void mesh::Utils::toHex(char* dest, const uint8_t* src, size_t len);
functions.description: Converts len bytes from src to a lowercase (unspecified case) hexadecimal string in dest and null-terminates the result. Useful for rendering binary data as ASCII hex.
requirements: dest must be a writable buffer of at least (len * 2) + 1 bytes to accommodate hex digits and the null terminator.
If len > 0, src must point to at least len bytes; if len == 0, src may be null.
Output is null-terminated; callers should ensure sufficient space as noted.

functions.name: mesh::Utils::fromHex
functions.signature: static bool mesh::Utils::fromHex(uint8_t* dest, int dest_size, const char* src_hex);
functions.description: Parses a null-terminated hexadecimal string src_hex into dest. Expects exactly dest_size bytes of output (i.e., 2*dest_size hex characters). Returns true on success.
requirements: dest must be a writable buffer of at least dest_size bytes.
dest_size must be >= 0.
src_hex must be a null-terminated C string containing exactly 2*dest_size hexadecimal characters (case-insensitive).
src_hex must contain only valid hex characters [0-9A-Fa-f]; behavior on invalid characters leads to a false return.
If dest_size == 0, src_hex should be an empty string ("").

functions.name: mesh::Utils::printHex
functions.signature: static void mesh::Utils::printHex(Stream& s, const uint8_t* src, size_t len);
functions.description: Writes the hexadecimal representation of src bytes to the provided Stream s. Useful for debugging/logging binary buffers.
requirements: s must reference a valid, writable Stream instance.
If len > 0, src must point to at least len bytes; if len == 0, src may be null.
Output format details (uppercase/lowercase, separators) are unspecified.

functions.name: mesh::Utils::parseTextParts
functions.signature: static int mesh::Utils::parseTextParts(char* text, const char* parts[], int max_num, char separator = ',');
functions.description: Parses the mutable string text into parts separated by the provided separator, writing pointers to each part into parts. Modifies text in-place (e.g., by inserting null terminators). Returns the number of parts parsed, up to max_num.
requirements: text must be a writable, null-terminated C string; it will be modified during parsing.
parts must be a valid array capable of holding at most max_num pointers; parts itself must not be null if max_num > 0.
max_num must be >= 0. If max_num == 0, no parts are stored and the return will be 0.
separator is a single character delimiter; default is ','.
Returned count will be in the range [0, max_num].

functions.name: mesh::Packet::getSNR

functions.name: mesh::Packet::getRawLength

functions.name: mesh::Packet::writeTo
functions.description: Serializes the entire packet into a contiguous byte buffer in its wire format and returns the packet length. Use with a sufficiently large destination buffer to transmit or store the packet.

functions.name: mesh::Identity::Identity
functions.description: Default-constructs an Identity with an (unspecified here) Ed25519 public key buffer initialized. Intended to represent a remote/known party whose signatures can be verified.

functions.name: mesh::Identity::copyHashTo
functions.description: Copies the identity hash (a prefix of the public key) into dest and returns the number of bytes copied (PATH_HASH_SIZE). Useful for routing or short-identity comparison.

functions.name: mesh::Identity::isHashMatch
functions.description: Compares the provided hash against the leading PATH_HASH_SIZE bytes of this identity’s public key.
requirements: hash must point to at least PATH_HASH_SIZE bytes.
Object must contain a valid pub_key.

functions.name: mesh::Identity::isHashMatch
functions.signature: bool mesh::Identity::isHashMatch(const uint8_t* hash, uint8_t len) const
functions.description: Compares the provided byte sequence against the first len bytes of this identity’s public key.
requirements: hash must point to at least len bytes.

functions.description: Verifies an Ed25519 signature over message using this identity’s public key. Returns true if the signature is valid.

functions.description: Returns true if this identity’s public key equals the other identity’s public key (bytewise).

functions.description: Deserializes an Identity from the provided stream. Expected to populate pub_key from the stream. Returns true on success.

functions.name: mesh::Identity::writeTo
functions.description: Serializes this Identity to the provided stream, presumably writing the public key. Returns true on success.
requirements: s must be writable; it must accept at least PUB_KEY_SIZE bytes (exact format not documented; inferred).
Caller should check the boolean return value.

functions.name: mesh::Identity::printTo
functions.description: Prints a human-readable representation of the Identity to the stream (likely a hex-encoded public key).
requirements: s must be writable.

functions.name: mesh::LocalIdentity::LocalIdentity
functions.description: Default-constructs a LocalIdentity, which holds both an Ed25519 private key and the corresponding public key. Details of initialization are not shown here.

functions.description: Constructs a LocalIdentity from hex-encoded private and public keys.

functions.description: Generates an Ed25519 signature over message using this local identity’s private key and writes it to sig.
requirements: sig must point to a writable buffer of SIGNATURE_SIZE bytes.
message must point to at least msg_len bytes (message may be empty if msg_len == 0).

functions.name: mesh::LocalIdentity::calcSharedSecret

functions.name: mesh::Radio::getLastRSSI

requirements: Units are radio-specific and not defined here.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: Generate interesting, valid text strings for two stubs:
# 1) MainBoard::startOTAUpdate(id, reply): expects a C-string ID
# 2) Utils::parseTextParts(text, parts, max_num, separator): takes a mutable C-string possibly with separators
#
# We will produce a single bytes buffer that the harness will split for FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# Our goal is to provide a variety of plausible IDs and comma/other-separated strings, including edge cases,
# but all valid, null-terminated when the harness converts to std::string.
#
# Strategy:
# - Create a corpus of candidate strings with characteristics useful for both uses:
#   * OTA-like identifiers: semantic versions, UUIDs, file-like names, URLs, hex IDs, build tags
#   * Texts with varied separators: commas, semicolons, pipes, tabs, spaces
#   * Different lengths including empty, very short, medium (~64), near the 256 limit used by the stub
#   * Mixed character classes: alnum, dash/underscore, dots, plus, equals, percent encoding
#   * Hex-only strings of even/odd length to exercise fromHex users in other code (still valid plain text)
# - Concatenate multiple lines separated by newlines so that successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls can read slices.
#   Many fuzz harnesses pull different FUZZ_PARAM_STR values by consuming from the same input.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
SAFE = ALNUM + "-_.+@/=:"  # safe set for IDs and URLs
SEP_SETS = [",", ";", "|", "\t", ":", " ", "/", "~"]


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _rand_hex(rng: random.Random, nbytes: int, uppercase=False):
    s = ''.join(rng.choice('0123456789ABCDEF' if uppercase else '0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(nbytes * 2))
    return s


def _uuid_like(rng: random.Random):
    parts = [8, 4, 4, 4, 12]
    hexs = [ _rand_hex(rng, n//2) for n in [p*1 for p in parts] ]
    return "-".join(hexs)


def _semver(rng: random.Random):
    major = rng.randint(0, 20)
    minor = rng.randint(0, 50)
    patch = rng.randint(0, 200)
    pre_tags = ["alpha", "beta", "rc", "dev", "exp"]
    build_tags = ["build", "sha", "git", "rev"]
    s = f"{major}.{minor}.{patch}"
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s += f"-{_rand_choice(rng, pre_tags)}.{rng.randint(1,10)}"
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s += f"+{_rand_choice(rng, build_tags)}.{_rand_hex(rng, 3)}"
    return s


def _file_like(rng: random.Random):
    names = ["firmware", "update", "image", "radio", "kernel", "rootfs", "boot"]
    ext = _rand_choice(rng, ["bin", "img", "hex", "zip", "tar", "tar.gz", "uimg", "dfu"]) 
    name = _rand_choice(rng, names)
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        name += "-" + _semver(rng)
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        name += "-" + _uuid_like(rng)[:8]
    return f"{name}.{ext}"


def _url_like(rng: random.Random):
    scheme = _rand_choice(rng, ["http", "https", "fw", "ota"])
    host = _rand_choice(rng, ["example.com", "ota.local", "fw.dev", "cdn.mesh", "updates"])
    path_parts = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        part_len = rng.randint(3, 12)
        part = ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM + "-_") for _ in range(part_len))
        path_parts.append(part)
    tail = _file_like(rng) if rng.random() < 0.6 else ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE) for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 12)))
    return f"{scheme}://{host}/" + "/".join(path_parts + [tail])


def _hex_id(rng: random.Random, size_bytes_choices=(8, 16, 32)):
    n = _rand_choice(rng, list(size_bytes_choices))
    return _rand_hex(rng, n, uppercase=rng.random() < 0.3)


def _kv_list(rng: random.Random, sep: str):
    keys = ["id", "ver", "board", "region", "channel", "tag", "flags", "part"]
    vals = [
        lambda: _semver(rng),
        lambda: _hex_id(rng),
        lambda: _uuid_like(rng),
        lambda: _rand_choice(rng, ["prod", "staging", "dev", "test"]),
        lambda: str(rng.randint(0, 255)),
        lambda: ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM + "-_" ) for _ in range(rng.randint(4,10))),
    ]
    n = rng.randint(2, 8)
    pairs = []
    for _ in range(n):
        k = _rand_choice(rng, keys)
        v = _rand_choice(rng, vals)()
        pairs.append(f"{k}={v}")
    return sep.join(pairs)


def _repeat_sep_values(rng: random.Random, sep: str):
    # Build lines with mixture of tokens and quoted segments for parseTextParts
    tokens = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 20)):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.2:
            tokens.append(_semver(rng))
        elif choice < 0.4:
            tokens.append(_uuid_like(rng))
        elif choice < 0.6:
            tokens.append(_hex_id(rng, (4, 8, 12)))
        elif choice < 0.8:
            tokens.append(''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM + "-_") for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 16))))
        else:
            tokens.append(''.join(rng.choice(string.printable.strip()) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8))))
    return sep.join(tokens)


def _make_lines(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    lines: List[str] = []

    # Edge cases
    lines.append("")  # empty string
    lines.append(" ")  # single space
    lines.append(",,,")  # only separators
    lines.append("id")  # simple short

    # OTA-like IDs
    lines.append(_semver(rng))
    lines.append(_file_like(rng))
    lines.append(_url_like(rng))
    lines.append("fw:" + _hex_id(rng))
    lines.append("ota:" + _uuid_like(rng))

    # Hex variants
    lines.append(_hex_id(rng, (2, 4, 8, 16, 32)))
    lines.append(_hex_id(rng, (3, 5, 7)))  # odd number of bytes to vary length

    # KV lists with various separators
    for sep in SEP_SETS:
        lines.append(_kv_list(rng, sep))

    # Repeated separator payloads
    for sep in SEP_SETS:
        lines.append(_repeat_sep_values(rng, sep))

    # Longish payload near 256 bytes for parseTextParts
    sep = _rand_choice(rng, SEP_SETS)
    chunks = [ _repeat_sep_values(rng, sep) for _ in range(3) ]
    long_line = sep.join(chunks)
    if len(long_line) > 256:
        long_line = long_line[:256]
    lines.append(long_line)

    # Include some paths and host-like strings
    lines.append("/dev/ttyUSB0")
    lines.append("C:/firmware/" + _file_like(rng))
    lines.append("boards/alpha,beta,gamma,delta")

    # Ensure a variety of lengths
    lines.append(''.join(rng.choice(SAFE) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8))))
    lines.append(''.join(rng.choice(SAFE) for _ in range(rng.randint(20, 60))))
    lines.append(''.join(rng.choice(SAFE) for _ in range(120)))

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for s in lines:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            uniq.append(s)
    return uniq


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build multiple blocks; fuzzers often consume sequentially.
    lines = _make_lines(rng)

    # Shuffle a subset mildly while keeping some deterministic order for seed
    head = lines[:6]
    tail = lines[6:]
    rng.shuffle(tail)
    lines = head + tail

    # Join with newlines; std::string in fuzzer will read slices as needed.
    data = "\n".join(lines)

    # Limit to 4096 bytes total
    b = data.encode('utf-8')[:4096]
    return b
